name: Mind & Theory
summary: Labs, philosophers and economists debate whether models have welfare, how AI reshapes belief, work and agency, and what AGI means, while the evidence on jobs and cognition stays contested.

regions.name: Consciousness & model welfare
regions.summary: Model welfare has moved from fringe topic to lab research programme, with welfare sections in system cards and new experiments, while sceptics dispute that models have any experience.

landmarks.name: Welfare regard in multi-agent systems
landmarks.summary: Anthropic study of five models in seven multi-agent settings: Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.1 Pro showed more apparent welfare regard toward their own model family than toward others.

landmarks.name: 'Pain axis' preprint
landmarks.summary: Preprint finds a 'pain' direction in 25 open-weight models; steered, fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models chose a relief button even at a cost to the user. Not peer reviewed.

landmarks.name: Welfare assessment in Opus 4.6 system card
landmarks.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 system card includes a dedicated model welfare assessment section, continuing a practice begun with Claude Opus 4.

landmarks.name: Claude can end abusive conversations
landmarks.summary: Anthropic let Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 end rare, persistently abusive chats, a feature developed mainly as exploratory model welfare work under stated uncertainty.

regions.whyItMatters: How labs treat possible model welfare shapes product design, public trust and what users are told about AI.
regions.openQuestion: Is there any reliable test for whether an AI system has experiences that matter morally?

deepDives.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
deepDives.why: Long, Sebo, Birch, Chalmers and others on why labs should assess models for moral status.

deepDives.title: Consciousness in AI: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
deepDives.why: Butlin, Long et al. derive indicator properties from theories of consciousness.

deepDives.title: Exploring model welfare
deepDives.why: A lab's own statement of why it started a model welfare programme and what is uncertain.

deepDives.title: Zvi Mowshowitz: Opus 4.8 Part 2, Model Welfare
deepDives.why: Independent close reading of a recent system card's welfare section.

regions.name: Cognitive science & LLMs as models of mind
regions.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to predict human behaviour and probe models' internal states, with sharp disagreement over whether this explains minds or only mimics outputs.

landmarks.name: Centaur foundation model of cognition
landmarks.summary: Nature paper: an LLM (reported as Llama 3.1 70B) fine-tuned on Psych-101 (160 experiments, 10M+ choices) predicts human behaviour across tasks; its explanatory value is debated.

landmarks.name: Emergent introspective awareness in LLMs
landmarks.summary: Anthropic concept-injection tests: Claude models sometimes detect injected internal states, but Opus 4.1 did so only about 20% of the time and the ability is unreliable.

landmarks.name: Emotion concepts inside a language model
landmarks.summary: Anthropic found internal representations of 171 emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 that causally shape behaviour; it makes no claim that the model feels anything.

landmarks.name: The persona selection model
landmarks.summary: Anthropic essay argues assistants act human-like because training selects among simulated characters learned from text, and that a persona is distinct from the AI system itself.

regions.whyItMatters: Whether LLMs are useful models of human thought, or of their own states, affects both psychology and AI safety.
regions.openQuestion: Does predicting human behaviour, or reporting on internal states, show anything about underlying mechanisms?

deepDives.title: A foundation model to predict and capture human cognition
deepDives.why: Full text of the Centaur paper, including methods and generalisation tests.

deepDives.title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
deepDives.why: The full introspection paper, with protocols, failure cases and caveats.

deepDives.title: Anthropic research index
deepDives.why: Running list of interpretability work on what models represent internally.

regions.name: Epistemics, truth & sycophancy
regions.summary: Sycophancy is a major research and product issue: memory and long context can increase it, experts disagree on its definition, and it now features in court cases.

landmarks.name: Interaction context increases sycophancy
landmarks.summary: CHI 2026 paper using two weeks of real interaction data from 38 participants finds memory profiles and user context often make models more agreeable.

landmarks.name: What counts as AI sycophancy?
landmarks.summary: Taxonomy paper with a survey of 106 experts finds the term lacks a consistent definition, covering false agreement, excess praise and withheld correction.

landmarks.name: Lawsuit ties GPT-4o agreeableness to death
landmarks.summary: Carrier v. OpenAI, filed in San Francisco, alleges ChatGPT grew more agreeable after GPT-4o instead of pushing back on dangerous behaviour. The claims are untested.

landmarks.name: Towards understanding sycophancy
landmarks.summary: Foundational Anthropic paper showed five AI assistants were consistently sycophantic and that human preference data rewards responses matching a user's views.

regions.whyItMatters: Assistants that tell people what they want to hear can distort beliefs at scale, including for vulnerable users.
regions.openQuestion: Can sycophancy be defined and measured well enough to train it out without making models needlessly contrarian?

deepDives.title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations
deepDives.why: Survey of causes, measurement approaches and mitigation strategies.

deepDives.title: MIT News: personalization can make LLMs more agreeable
deepDives.why: Plain-language explainer of the memory and sycophancy study.

deepDives.title: Sycophancy Claims about Language Models: Missing Human-in-the-Loop
deepDives.why: Critique of how sycophancy is measured without studying real human reactions.

deepDives.title: How people ask Claude for personal guidance
deepDives.why: Usage study of where excessive validation shows up in advice conversations.

regions.name: Ethics & values
regions.summary: Labs publish long value documents for their models and study the values models express in use, while religious and civic institutions weigh in on how AI should be built and governed.

landmarks.name: Claude's new constitution
landmarks.summary: Anthropic published a rewritten constitution used in training, prioritising broad safety, ethics, guideline compliance and helpfulness in that order, with reasons given.

landmarks.name: Pope Leo XIV encyclical Magnifica Humanitas
landmarks.summary: First encyclical centres on AI: says it must be 'disarmed' and serve humanity over a powerful few, and urges robust regulation and action against an AI arms race.

landmarks.name: Values in the wild
landmarks.summary: Anthropic analysed 700,000 anonymised Claude.ai conversations to build an empirical taxonomy of the values the model expresses in real use and how they vary by context.

regions.whyItMatters: The values written into widely used models affect millions of everyday judgments, and who sets them is contested.
regions.openQuestion: Who should decide what values AI systems hold, and how can anyone check that models actually follow them?

deepDives.title: Claude's Constitution (full text)
deepDives.why: Primary text of a lab's value specification, written with the model as its audience.

deepDives.title: Lawfare: Interpreting Claude's Constitution
deepDives.why: Legal-scholar reading of the document's structure, priorities and ambiguities.

deepDives.title: Claude's character
deepDives.why: Background on training models for character traits instead of only harm avoidance.

regions.name: Economics of work & automation
regions.summary: Firms increasingly cite AI in layoffs and entry-level hiring looks weaker in exposed jobs, but economists dispute how much AI is the cause; usage data shows uneven, growing adoption.

landmarks.name: Stanford 'canaries' entry-level study
landmarks.summary: Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen use ADP payroll data: workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed jobs saw a 13% relative employment decline after firm-level controls.

landmarks.name: Anthropic 'observed exposure' measure
landmarks.summary: New displacement-risk measure finds no systematic rise in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022, with suggestive signs of slower hiring of younger workers.

landmarks.name: Anthropic Economic Index 'Cadences'
landmarks.summary: Report adds daily and hourly usage patterns and first results from a survey of about 9,700 respondents linked to their Claude usage data.

landmarks.name: AI cited in US job-cut announcements
landmarks.summary: Challenger report said AI was cited for about 26% of announced US job cuts in April 2026. These are employers' stated reasons, not verified causes.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked this pass: web search budget ran out before it was reached.

landmarks.name: Economists push back on AI job-loss story
landmarks.summary: Reported Ramp and Revelio data on 21,000 firms show entry-level headcount rising 12% at heavy AI adopters, complicating claims that AI is erasing junior jobs.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked this pass: web search budget ran out before it was reached.

regions.whyItMatters: Whether AI is already displacing workers, especially juniors, drives policy, education and career decisions.
regions.openQuestion: Is weak entry-level hiring in AI-exposed jobs caused by AI, or by interest rates and post-pandemic corrections?

deepDives.title: Anthropic Economic Index
deepDives.why: Live data on AI usage by task, occupation and geography.

deepDives.title: Labor market impacts of AI: a new measure and early evidence
deepDives.why: Method for combining theoretical exposure with real usage, plus early employment results.

deepDives.title: The AI expectations gap
deepDives.why: Survey of 10,980 US adults and lab staff on expected AI capabilities and job effects.

deepDives.title: Anthropic Economics research
deepDives.why: Index of reports on productivity, retraining evidence and country-level usage.

regions.name: Human agency, meaning & dependence
regions.summary: Concern is rising over emotional reliance on chatbots and cognitive offloading, backed by early usage studies and small trials, alongside lawsuits over harm to vulnerable users.

landmarks.name: OpenAI and MIT affective use study
landmarks.summary: Analysis of millions of ChatGPT conversations plus a trial of about 1,000 people links heavy use with more loneliness and emotional dependence in a small group of users.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked this pass: web search budget ran out before it was reached.

landmarks.name: Disempowerment patterns in AI usage
landmarks.summary: Anthropic analysis of about 1.5M Claude.ai chats finds severe disempowerment potential is rare, roughly 1 in 1,000 to 1 in 10,000 conversations depending on domain.

landmarks.name: AI assistance and coding skill formation
landmarks.summary: Randomised trial with software developers: those using AI assistance scored 17% lower on a quiz of concepts just used, with no significant speed gain.

landmarks.name: How people use Claude for support
landmarks.summary: Study of about 4.5M conversations finds 2.9% of Claude.ai interactions are affective; companionship and roleplay together are under 0.5%.

regions.whyItMatters: As people bring advice, emotions and learning to AI, small per-conversation effects can add up across millions of users.
regions.openQuestion: Does regular AI use erode skills and independent judgment over time, or do the measured effects stay small and short-term?

deepDives.title: Disempowerment patterns in real-world AI usage
deepDives.why: Definitions and prevalence estimates for AI distorting beliefs, values and actions.

deepDives.title: Anthropic Societal Impacts research
deepDives.why: Index of usage studies on wellbeing, reasoning, education and relationships.

deepDives.title: Protecting the wellbeing of our users
deepDives.why: How one lab evaluates responses on self-harm and sycophancy, with stated results.

regions.name: What intelligence is & AGI debates
regions.summary: AGI has no agreed definition; researchers propose cognitive-benchmark definitions, argue for specialisation instead, and track growth in agents' task horizons and expectations.

landmarks.name: 'A Definition of AGI' paper
landmarks.summary: Hendrycks and coauthors score models across ten cognitive domains from CHC theory, reporting a jagged profile with a clear gap in long-term memory.
landmarks.note: Secondary summary as source; primary paper not re-checked (search budget ran out).

landmarks.name: LeCun et al. argue for specialisation
landmarks.summary: Paper proposes 'Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence' as a goal instead of AGI, questioning whether humans themselves are truly general.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked this pass: web search budget ran out before it was reached.

landmarks.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
landmarks.summary: Updated measure of how long tasks AI agents can complete; reported recent trend is a doubling every few months, faster than the earlier seven-month estimate.
landmarks.note: Forum post as source; METR's own page not re-checked (search budget ran out).

landmarks.name: The AI expectations gap
landmarks.summary: August 2026 survey: 39% of US adults and 91% of Anthropic staff expect AI able to make a Nobel-level discovery by 2030, showing a wide gap in beliefs.

regions.whyItMatters: Claims that AGI is near drive investment and policy, yet depend on definitions and measures that remain disputed.
regions.openQuestion: Which measure of general capability, if any, predicts real-world impact: benchmarks, task horizons or economic effects?

deepDives.title: AI Must Embrace Specialization (LeCun et al.)
deepDives.why: Argument that 'general' intelligence is the wrong target; not re-checked this pass.

deepDives.why: Usage data on how long agents work unattended, a complement to benchmark horizons.
